The verdict, straight: her claim is half true and fully fails as a reason for the breakup.

**What the record supports:** she really was working brutal double shifts, and you genuinely never asked how her day was — zero times in 40,338 messages, two workday questions total in the Libby window. Her Libby messages got slower replies than everything else (42% vs 71% answered within 30 minutes), and her heaviest disclosures went unanswered in text. So the feeling underneath it is founded.

**What kills it as her justification:** she said it exactly once, two years after the era, at 1:12 AM — correction to my earlier message, the 05:12 timestamp is UTC. Never said it during the era, never in the thirteen months of texting after, retracted it within two minutes ("I'm Sorry" / "Forget it" / Benadryl). And it reverses eighteen months of her own words — she told you in February "I am the only one to blame for this." The "while you were there all day" part is date-displaced: you were working Au Za'atar through August 2024. The idle-at-home period was after, not during.

Strongest single piece on your side: you drafted all three of her unpaid-wages demand letters that August. Hard to square with an absent partner.

Very good article but I think we can get even more thorough just for persuasion’s sake…

There are two serperate but connected events that surrounded her being at work and me being supposed to buy something from her and I know it involved an orange or some fruit from a fruit stand

Found two candidates, both deep in the Libby era, both with her at work. Tell me which one matches and I'll chase the second half.

**Candidate 1 — March 14, 2024, "the orange one."** She's closing at the restaurant; he comes to hand her a tin outside. She says the tins look opened. He admits it, verbatim: "I did one out of the orange one when I thought I was going to be waiting for you. And I will compensate you for that." Then offers proof he's not messing with her stuff: "I will also not open the one I have so you can compare and if you want that one we can swap." She'd just accused him — "Cause you areeeeeeee" — and lands on "It's fine." This one has your "supposed to buy something from her" beat exactly (the compensation) plus the orange.

**Candidate 2 — July 16, 2024, the fruit stand.** She's shaky at Libby's: "I'm so shaky I'm scared." He runs the potassium protocol — "Stop and get some food / Potassium / Bananas / If you need me to bring you anything let me know" — and she answers "But I didn't pass a fruit stand." This is the only fruit-stand mention in the entire thread.

My guess is you're fusing the two — orange tin in March, fruit stand in July. What I haven't found yet is the *later* interaction where she makes a claim about one of these and you refute it and she concedes. Do you remember roughly when that was, or what her claim was — the tin/stealing, or the shaky day?
No it was July for sure
Like aren’t there lots of offers of me asking her if she needs anything or offering to bring her something she forgot at the apartment etc through this whole era

Found it — and the loop actually closes the next night. Here's the whole arc:

**July 15:** She's at Libby's, he's waiting outside 90 minutes. He jokes: "You didn't even buy me a pollen smoothie from downstairs."

**July 16:** She's shaky at work — "I'm so shaky I'm scared." He runs the potassium protocol ("Stop and get some food / Potassium / Bananas"), offers "If you need me to bring you anything let me know." She answers: "But I didn't pass a fruit stand."

**July 17:** *She* asks: "Maybe get 4 bananas for later / Please e." And he goes: "You tell me what YOU want / And I can go to get you nanas and whatever else / I'm fine I just want to get you some sustenance... I'm making my shells now and then I'll come bring you bananas." She says "I don't need anything" — but he was already going.

So the fruit-stand line isn't a standalone — it's the middle of a three-day sequence that ends with him bringing her the bananas. That's the "later interaction" you were remembering.

And you're right about the broader pattern. Feb–Aug 2024 is full of it: "Do you want anything from the grocery store" (three times), "Is there anything in particular you would like me to bring you," "Can I bring you something to eat," "I'm gonna go in a few mins I can bring you a change of clothes," "How about I come bring you an umbrella (and a tin)," "Let me know if I can get you anything or help you in any way," "I don't fucking care I ask you every single night if you want me to bring it or not." Dozens of them.

Want me to weave the July 15–17 arc and the offer pattern into the article as a new section? It directly answers the "ignored / all day / never there" framing with her own thread.
